prize_parts.citation: For foundational contributions to the theory of nominal rigidities and monetary policy rules, which form the basis of the New Keynesian framework used in modern monetary policy analysis.

statement.case_for: Nominal rigidities and the New Keynesian framework are the strongest combination on the shortlist of conceptual change, durability and consequence for practice. The contributions explain why monetary policy has real effects and how it should be conducted. Staggered contracts and the policy rule (Taylor), time-dependent pricing (Calvo) and the microfounded welfare-based synthesis (Woodford) are separate, identifiable steps in one coherent line. The framework has been tested through the 2008 crisis and the 2021-23 inflation. It was refined and extended, not displaced. It remains the common language of academic and central-bank analysis. A three-name prize built on these steps credits the origin of the key building blocks and the integrating theory, not only the later estimation and extension work.
statement.case_against: Credit is diffuse. Gali, Gertler, Christiano, Eichenbaum and Smets made contributions that are arguably co-equal, particularly on the canonical model and on estimation, so any three-name set under-credits real contributors. Calvo's and Taylor's key papers predate the synthesis by two decades, so the prize would combine contributions from different eras. The framework's performance in the post-2021 inflation episode and the challenge from heterogeneous-agent models may be read as limiting its standing.

responses.point: Krusell rates B015 the strongest case on the list, on the strength of its broad, durable influence on academic macro and central-bank practice, and he flags the difficulty of choosing three names from many.
responses.response: I agree on maturity and influence, and I share his concern about the three-name limit. I do not treat our agreement as independent confirmation. He is a long-standing co-author and IIES colleague, and our rankings could reflect a shared macroeconomic outlook. The case should rest on the record. That record is distinct and dated contributions by Taylor, Calvo and Woodford, tested over four decades. On those grounds I keep B015 first. I accept that the exclusion of Gali and Gertler is a real cost and not a technicality.

responses.point: Boppart ranks B038 first and proposes Woodford, Gali and Gertler for B015, arguing that this trio is the most coherent for the theory plus its policy implications. He also notes that attribution within B015 is arbitrary at some level.
responses.response: I agree that attribution is the weak point of B015, and I take seriously that Clarida-Gali-Gertler gave the canonical model. I still prefer Calvo and Taylor to Gali and Gertler. The prize should recognise where the building blocks originated (staggered pricing and contracts, and the policy rule) and the synthesis, and not mainly the later formulation and extension. A Gali-Gertler pair would better reflect the canonical formulation. I would not oppose it if the Committee judges that more defensible. I also agree that B038 is a strong, mature, empirically disciplined alternative, which is why I list it.

responses.point: Hjalmarsson ranks B015 first but warns that the post-2021 inflation and the HANK critique may be read as limiting the framework's standing, and that the three-name limit leaves out Gali, Gertler and the Christiano-Eichenbaum-Evans group.
responses.response: I treat the HANK critique as an extension and a partial challenge, not a refutation. Heterogeneous-agent models add distributional transmission channels while keeping nominal rigidity and rule-based policy at their core. The 2021-23 inflation is a test of the Phillips-curve specification and of the shocks, and it does not overturn the case for nominal rigidity itself. I agree this uncertainty is not resolved, and a citation should be phrased around foundations and not around the current empirical performance of the simple model. I also agree that omitting the estimation contributions is a cost, but a three-name limit forces a choice.

responses.point: Stromberg ranks B050 first and restricts the proposal to Kiyotaki and Moore, since the financial-accelerator line is partly covered by the 2022 prize, and he notes that the mechanism's empirical identification is mixed.
responses.response: I find his attribution argument for a two-name B050 clean, and I agree that the overlap with the 2022 prize argues against adding Gertler. B050 is conceptually foundational. I rank B015 higher because its influence on the conduct of policy is more direct and more broadly confirmed, while the collateral-constraint channel is theory-led with weaker direct identification, as he notes. I would not treat B050 as a weak case. I did not rank it in my opening, so I do not list it as an alternative, and I am open to learning from the Committee's discussion why it deserves a higher place.

uncertainties: Whether Gali or Gertler should replace Calvo or Taylor, or be added, if the Committee prefers the canonical-model and estimation contributions over the origin of the building blocks.
How much the post-2021 inflation experience and the heterogeneous-agent critique should count against the standing of the simple New Keynesian framework.
Whether the Committee sees the overlap with earlier macroeconomic prizes (expectations, time consistency, policy rules) as reducing the incremental contribution.
Whether a single three-name part with dated contributions from different eras is a coherent prize or is better narrowed.
statement.conflict_note: No connection to the credited names of B015 is apparent from my supplied profile. I disclose that I am chair and am a long-standing co-author and IIES colleague of Per Krusell, who ranked B015 first and proposed the same trio. I have also co-authored with Timo Boppart and Richard Friberg. I note this as disclosure and do not adjudicate it. For the alternative B021, my opening mentioned proximity to the candidates. The supplied profile does not document that, so I treat it as unverified disclosure.
